mechanism: Work in the exact coconductor (Ramanujan-packet) coordinates that the wheel modulus Q_k already forces: the finite additive spectrum of Z/Q_k partitions by q = Q_k/gcd(r, Q_k), each packet q | Q_k carrying the complete Ramanujan kernel c_q, and the zero mode q = 1 is the self-coupling already eliminated exactly with contraction rho < 1/6. Expand the centered response H_{k,n} = C − 2E in these packets as a single isometric (Parseval) decomposition — not a triangle-inequality split — so the Gram value over the window r < H becomes an exact double sum over packet pairs (q, q') of window correlation kernels times signed amplitudes. The decisive structural fact is the square sampling: X_{N+r} = (N+r+1)² − 1 makes every window phase at a rational frequency b/m, m = lcm(q, q') | Q_k, a quadratic exponential sum in r, which is evaluated (complete case) or completed (incomplete case) by classical quadratic Gauss sums with EXACT modulus-square-root size: |window kernel| ≤ min(H, C·√m·log m·(1 + H/m)). This is the constructed map demanded by obstacle 2: off-diagonal pair ↦ shared modulus m = lcm(q,q') | Q_k, with pair multiplicity 3^{ω(m)} and kernel size m^{1/2} — sub-square multiplicity, and total packet count τ(Q_k) ≈ 2^k = X^{o(1)} so packet combinatorics costs only a divisor-bound loss. On the diagonal, the packet-q mass is the dispersion of the prime comb over residues mod q; for large smooth q (q > X^δ) this is controlled by Selberg/Brun–Titchmarsh upper bounds on prime-pair counts at spacings jq (upper bounds only — no parity issue), with the wheel weights 1/(q·φ(q)) making the aggregate converge. The unconditionally hard content is thereby compressed into the small-denominator packets q ≤ X^δ, where I invoke the renewal structure: the classical exact identity Σ_{d≤y} c_d(n) = Σ_{e|n} e·M(y/e), matched against the kernel-checked reindexing of E as the Mertens-weighted reciprocal family, says the small-q amplitude of H should be an exact rescaled copy of the same centered response at the contracted scale ~X/q — closing by induction across blocks against the exact contraction rho < 1/6, with signed spectral data inserted rather than |M(d)|. The pinned start L_k = W_{k-1} enters as an exact simplification, not an obstruction: e(L_k·a/q) = 1 for every q | W_{k-1}, so all packet phase offsets collapse at precisely the synchronized start.
new_leverage: Three things a standard application does not give. (1) The square sampling X_n = (n+1)² − 1 is not decoration: at rational wheel frequencies it turns every off-diagonal window correlation into a quadratic Gauss sum with exact √m cancellation — an identity-level evaluation, not an estimate — supplying precisely the "map from off-diagonal pairs to a shared modulus with sub-square multiplicity" that obstacle 2 declares unknown, with shared modulus lcm(q,q') | Q_k and multiplicity 3^{ω(m)}·m^{1/2} ≪ m^{1/2+o(1)} against trivial m. (2) The split is orthogonal/isometric, so the C − 2E correlation is carried into each packet as a single signed amplitude rather than destroyed by a triangle inequality across C and E — the packet's requested "exact transformation preserving the C − 2E correlation" is the coconductor transform itself (already exact algebra in PrimeWheelCoconductorGram.lean; my contribution is the analytic evaluation layer on top). (3) The renewal identity Σ_{d≤y} c_d(n) = Σ_{e|n} e·M(y/e) aligns the Ramanujan packets with the kernel-checked Mertens-weighted reciprocal family, converting the small-q hard core into the SAME statement at scale X/q, which is the only shape that can legitimately exploit the rho < 1/6 contraction — turning strong induction from a failed absolute-value operator bound (obstacle 4) into a signed fixed-point/contraction argument.
target_estimate: Named estimate: Wheel Coconductor Dispersion Lemma (WCDL). Variables: k-th primorial wheel, modulus Q = Q_k > 6·U_k; packets q | Q, q > 1; window N, H with 1 ≤ H ≤ N; samples X_{N+r} = (N+r+1)² − 1 all inside the synchronized block (W_{k-1}, W_k]; A_q(x) = the exact coconductor amplitude of H at packet q (repo object primeWheelCoconductorComponent with zero mode excluded). Claim, in two provable halves plus one reduction: (i) OFF-DIAGONAL (unconditional): |Σ_{q≠q'} signed cross Gram terms| ≪ X^{o(1)} · (Σ_q Σ_{r<H} |A_q(X_{N+r})|²) · max_{m=lcm(q,q')} min(1, √m·log m·(1+H/m)/H), with the X^{o(1)} = τ(Q)^{O(1)} = exp(O(log X·log 2/loglog X)) divisor loss and the √m from complete/completed quadratic Gauss sums — loss factor X^{o(1)} total, compatible with rung 2's ε. (ii) LARGE-q DIAGONAL (unconditional): for q | Q with q > X^δ, Σ_{r<H} |A_q(X_{N+r})|² ≪_δ H·X^{1+ε}·q^{-1}·(q/φ(q)) via Selberg upper-sieve prime-pair counts at spacings jq; summed over q | Q, q > X^δ this is ≪ H·X^{1+ε}·X^{-δ(1-ε)} — negligible. (iii) REDUCTION (the compressed core, conjectural): target holds iff the small-packet renewal bound holds: for q | Q, 1 < q ≤ X^δ, |A_q(X)| ≪_ε q^{-1+ε}·(X)^{1/2+ε}, to be proved by the renewal reindexing A_q(X) = (exact Mertens-weighted recombination of H at scale ≤ X/q) + O(X^{1/2+ε}), then induction across blocks against rho < 1/6. Total loss budget: X^{o(1)} from divisor counts and Gauss-sum logs, constant from the 2-adic Gauss-sum case (Q even), summable-in-k block losses required additive, not multiplicative.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Engaged directly, and the pin is used as leverage: no translation averaging is invoked anywhere — Ramanujan kernels and quadratic Gauss sums are exact complete-sum identities valid at the specific start, and at L_k = W_{k-1} the phase offsets e(L_k a/q) collapse to 1 for every q | W_{k-1}, so the synchronized start is the spectrally simplest point of the block, not a possible exceptional one. No exceptional-set language appears; nothing needs W_{k-1} excluded from anything.
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: This is the obstacle the angle attacks head-on: the square sampling converts off-diagonal packet pairs (q,q') into complete quadratic Gauss sums to the shared modulus m = lcm(q,q') | Q_k, with multiplicity 3^{omega(m)}·m^{1/2} ≪ m^{1/2+o(1)} against trivial m — exactly the previously unconstructed sub-square-multiplicity map. This half is unconditional, checkable by finite computation, and worth extracting even if the rest dies.
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Agreed and respected: no averaging over varying moduli is used. Moduli appear only as the fixed divisor lattice of Q_k; where prime-in-AP dispersion enters (large-q diagonal), it is per-fixed-q via one-sided sieve pair-count upper bounds, which need no BV input; the middle/small-q range is deliberately NOT handled by per-q dispersion (which provably stalls at O(x²/φ(q)) without averaging) but rerouted through the renewal reduction.
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: Position: the failure mode is inserting |M(d)| with absolute values; this angle inserts signed packet amplitudes and closes by contraction, not domination — the induction hypothesis enters once per block, additively in energy, against the exact factor rho < 1/6. Honest caveat: if the per-block X^{o(1)} losses compound multiplicatively across the induction they sum to exp((log X)^{3/2}/polyloglog) and the argument dies; closure requires the renewal inequality to be additive in block energies, which is plausible from the Gram structure but is the second-weakest link and is stated as such.
obstacle_positions.parity: Sieve machinery is used only for upper bounds on prime-pair counts (large-q diagonal), where parity does not bind. The angle is not sieve-only: its core operations are exact character-sum evaluations (Ramanujan, Gauss) and a signed renewal identity. Parity is displaced, not defeated: the irreducible RH-strength content survives in the small-q signed amplitudes, as it must for an RH-equivalent target — the angle's claim is compression of the hard core, not evasion of it.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: All numerics in this angle are kill-only: the decomposition identities are exact (they hold or fail, no scaling inference), and the one scaling computation proposed (small-q amplitude growth) is used solely to falsify — raw prime-discrepancy scaling kills the angle; square-root-looking scaling is explicitly treated as non-evidence and transfers no weight to the proof obligation. Rung 0 must close by proof (Siegel–Walfisz), not by extrapolated exponents.

kill_test: One-day computation at k = 3 or 4 (W = 30 or 210, Q_k the repo's minimal admissible modulus > 6·U_k). (a) Verify exactness: compute H_{k,n} from the kernel-checked C − 2E identity and independently from the coconductor packet sum with zero mode removed; any mismatch kills the coordinate claim immediately. (b) The decisive test: compute the exact small-packet amplitudes A_q(X_n) for q ∈ {2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30} across n with X_n up to ~10^6 (direct sieve, complete sums — cheap), and compare their growth against two templates: renewal scale (X/q)^{1/2}·polylog versus raw per-character prime-discrepancy scale psi(X;q,b) − X/φ(q) computed on the same data. If the small-q amplitudes of H track the raw discrepancy scale — i.e., the orthogonal split loses the C − 2E correlation packet-by-packet exactly as the triangle inequality does — the renewal core is dead and with it the angle (only the unconditional off-diagonal Gauss-sum lemma survives as a tool). Secondary cheap check: numerically confirm the off-diagonal window kernels at a few (q,q') pairs match the min(H, √m·log m·(1+H/m)) prediction for the actual incomplete windows H ≤ N ≪ √m arising in-range.
rung0_plan: Rung 0 closes with the same machinery and no new ideas: (1) exact coconductor partition and zero-mode elimination (already formalized); (2) small packets q ≤ (log X)^A: bound each amplitude by Siegel–Walfisz for the prime comb mod q — uniform in q in this range and uniform in the pinned block since the bound is per-modulus, giving A_q ≪ X·exp(−c√log X); (3) packets q > (log X)^A: trivial amplitude bound plus the wheel weight decay 1/(q·φ(q)) summed over divisors of Q gives ≪ X²/(log X)^{A(1−ε)} for the energy; (4) off-diagonal by the trivial per-pair bound H·A_q·A_{q'} with τ(Q) = X^{o(1)} packet count. Net: |H_{k,n}| ≪ X/(log X)^A for every fixed A — o(X) at PNT strength, uniform over synchronized blocks and square samples. Every ingredient is classical and per-modulus, so the pinned start costs nothing. This is the viability control: the angle's coordinates already reproduce PNT strength without touching the renewal conjecture.
plausible_partial: Realistic within bounded effort, in decreasing confidence: (1) The off-diagonal Gauss-sum lemma (WCDL part i) as a standalone unconditional theorem, plausibly Lean-formalizable since complete quadratic Gauss sum evaluation is finite algebra plus a classical modulus-square-root identity — this resolves the constructive gap named in obstacle 2 regardless of the angle's fate. (2) Full rung-0 closure |H_{k,n}| ≪_A X/(log X)^A with explicit uniformity in the pinned block. (3) The large-q diagonal estimate (WCDL part ii) via Selberg pair counts, unconditional. (4) A clean reduction theorem: the full rung-2 target follows from the small-packet renewal bound |A_q(X)| ≪_ε q^{−1+ε} X^{1/2+ε} for q | Q_k, q ≤ X^δ — an unconditional compression of the RH-hard content into smooth small moduli with the signed structure intact. NOT plausible at bounded effort: any unconditional fixed exponent θ < 1 (rung 1), since the fixed-small-q amplitudes are capped at PNT strength by everything known — consistent with the fact that even M(x) ≪ x^θ, θ < 1, is open.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely to be false: that the orthogonal coconductor split preserves the C − 2E cancellation inside each small-q packet — i.e., that A_q(X) for fixed small q is renewal-scale (~(X/q)^{1/2}) rather than raw prime-discrepancy scale (~X·exp(−c√log X)). Orthogonality preserves total energy and signs globally, but each packet amplitude is a single linear functional of C and E, and nothing in Parseval forces their correlation to survive into an individual frequency; if it does not, the angle reproduces exactly the separate-bounding failure the route document warns against, merely in a prettier basis, and only the unconditional off-diagonal lemma and rung 0 survive. The kill test targets this assumption first and costs about a day.
